S5.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
S5.text: 6. Correlation and Regression Correlation measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables. The Pearson correlation coefficient r ranges from -1 to +1. A value near +1 indicates a strong positive linear relationship, near -1 a strong negative one and near 0 no linear relationship. Correlation does not imply causation: a hidden confounding variable may drive both variables. Simple linear regression fits the line y-hat = b0 + b1 * x by least squares, which minimizes the sum of squared residuals. The slope b1 equals r * (s_y / s_x) and the intercept is b0 = y-bar - b1 * x-bar. The coefficient of determination R squared is the proportion of variance in y explained by the model; in simple regression it equals r squared. Residual plots should show no pattern; curved or funnel-shaped residuals indicate a violated assumption.
